newsitem.title: USA: United Healthcare profits rise, but stock falls.
newsitem.headline: United Healthcare profits rise, but stock falls.

text.p: United Healthcare Corp. said its profits rose 33 percent in the second quarter, but the nation's leading health maintenance company said certain of its businesses fared poorly and threatened to erode full-year results.
That admission drove the company's stock down $7.375 to $50.69 at mid-afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the third most active issue.
United Healthcare said earnings for the quarter rose to $116 million from $87 million in the same year-ago period.
Earnings per share rose to 57 cents, in line with Wall Street estimates and up from 43 cents a share, excluding special items, a year earlier.

But the Minneapolis-based health maintenance organisation said profit margins lagged in Maryland, Rhode Island and the Gulf Coast, reducing net income in the second quarter by about 6 cents a share and posing a threat to earnings for the remainder of the year.

"We are of course pleased with the progress made during the second quarter," said Chairman William W. McGuire. "However, we are now focusing significant resources to ensure improved performance in a few health plan markets...in which we have not yet reached margins achieved in aggregate by our other health plans."
"While improved performance is expected in these markets, the performance at these health plans will continue to be a drag on earnings for the remainder of 1997," he added.
The company said revenues for the second quarter rose 18 percent, to $2.9 billion.
Signs of declining HMO enrollment, coupled with concern over rising medical costs, have weighed heavily on health care stocks this week.
On Tuesday, Aetna Inc., one of the country's biggest health insurers, saw its stock tumble more than 10 percent after it reported slower-than-expected growth in its HMO and Medicare plans.
